content: 1. Kinlock TW, Gordon MS, et al. (2009) conducted a randomized clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of methadone maintenance therapy for prisoners. The study assessed outcomes six months after release and was published in the Journal of Substance Abuse Treatment, volume 37, issue 3, pages 277-285. 2. Garcia CA, Correa GC, et al. (2007) investigated the use of buprenorphine-naloxone treatment for opioid-dependent inmates in Puerto Rico prior to their release. The findings were published in the Journal of Addiction Medicine, volume 1, issue 3, pages 126-132. 3. Hedrich D, Alves P, et al. (2012) conducted a systematic review to assess the effectiveness of opioid maintenance treatment in prison settings. The results were published in Addiction, volume 107, issue 3, pages 501-517. 4. Sacks JY, McKendrick K, et al. (2012) performed a randomized clinical trial to evaluate therapeutic community treatment for female inmates. Outcomes were measured at six and twelve months post-release and published in the Journal of Addictive Diseases, volume 31, issue 3, pages 258-269. 5. Springer SA, Chen S, et al. (2010) examined the impact of buprenorphine treatment on improving HIV and substance abuse treatment outcomes for HIV-infected prisoners after release. The study was published in the Journal of Urban Health, volume 87, issue 4, pages 592-602. 6. The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) (2013) reported on the implementation of opioid substitution treatment (OST) in Tihar prisons, India. This scientific report was published by UNODC in Vienna. 7. Freudenberg N, Ramaswamy M, et al. (2010) evaluated the REAL MEN re-entry program, which aimed to reduce drug use, HIV risk, and recidivism among young men leaving jail. The findings were published in the Journal of Adolescent Health, volume 47, issue 5, pages 448-455. 8. De la Fuente L, Bravo MJ, et al. (2012) analyzed the evolution of opioid substitution treatment and needle exchange programs in Spanish prisons from 1992 to 2009. The study was published in the Spanish Journal of Penitentiary Health, volume 14, issue 2, pages 67-77. 9. Bachireddy C, Bazazi AR, et al. (2011) explored attitudes toward opioid substitution therapy and pre-incarceration HIV transmission behaviors among HIV-infected prisoners in Malaysia. The study highlighted implications for secondary prevention and was published in Drug and Alcohol Dependence, volume 116, issues 1-3, pages 151-157. 10. Favrod-Coune T, Baroundi M, et al. (2013) presented a case study on opioid substitution treatment in pretrial prison detention in Geneva, Switzerland. The findings were published in the Swiss Medical Weekly, volume 143. 11. Eshrati B, Asl RT, et al. (2008) provided initial support for harm reduction education to prevent HIV transmission among Iranian prisoners. The study was published in the Harm Reduction Journal, volume 5, article 21. 12. Derlega VJ, Winstead BA, et al. (2008) examined the stigma associated with AIDS among inmates and staff in a U.S. state prison. The findings were published in the Journal of STD and AIDS, volume 19, issue 4, pages 259-263. 13. Fields J, Gonzalez I, et al. (2008) discussed insights gained from working with incarcerated women. 14. Sifunda S, Reddy PS, et al. (2008) evaluated the effectiveness of a peer-led HIV/AIDS and STI health education intervention for prison inmates. The study was published in Health Education and Behavior, volume 35, issue 4, pages 494-508. 15. Ko NY, Hsu ST, et al. (2009) conducted a pilot study on the impact of HIV education on substance use readiness to change, AIDS knowledge, and self-efficacy for risk reduction among male drug-dependent inmates. The findings were published in Substance Use and Misuse, volume 44, issue 3, pages 322-331. 16. Grinstead O, Eldridge G, et al. (2008) implemented Project START, an HIV, STD, and hepatitis prevention program for young men leaving prison. The study was published in the Journal of Correctional Health Care, volume 17, issue 8, pages 2676-2684. 17. Fluhmann P, Wassmer M, et al. (2012) examined structured information exchange on infectious diseases for prisoners. The study was published in the Journal of Correctional Health Care, volume 18, issue 3, pages 198-209. 18. Goldberg E, Millson P, et al. (2009) conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate an HIV risk reduction intervention for incarcerated youth. The study was published in the Journal of Adolescent Health, volume 44, issue 2, pages 136-145. 19. Gurdin J, Niego S, et al. (2008) described the Rikers Health Advocacy Program (RHAP), an STI/HIV/AIDS prevention program for young men, in the book Model Programs for Adolescent Sexual Health: Evidence-Based HIV, STI, and Pregnancy Prevention Interventions, pages 263-271. 20. Hurd NM, Valerio MN, et al. (2010) adapted an HIV prevention intervention for high-risk, incarcerated adolescents. The study was published in Health Education and Behavior, volume 37, issue 1, pages 37-50. 21. Martin S, O’Connell D, et al. (2008) integrated an HIV/HCV brief intervention into prisoner re-entry programs. The results of this multisite prospective study were published in the Journal of Psychoactive Drugs, volume 40, issue 4, pages 427-436. 22. La Vigne NG, Debus-Sherrill S, et al. (2011) explored situational crime prevention approaches to reduce violence and sexual assault in jail. The findings were published in the Justice Policy Center Brief. 23. Yap L, Richters J, et al. (2011) documented the decline in sexual assaults in men’s prisons in New South Wales using a systems approach. The study was published in the Journal of Interpersonal Violence, volume 26, issue 15, pages 3157-3181. 24. Ravi A, Blankenship KM, et al. (2007) addressed women’s health issues in incarceration, published in Women’s Health Issues, volume 17, issue 4, pages 210-216. 25. Kerbs JJ, Jolley JM (2007) investigated inmate-on-inmate victimization among older male prisoners. The study was published in Crime and Delinquency, volume 31, issue 5, pages 385-393. 26. Kavasery R, Maru DS, et al. (2009) conducted a prospective controlled trial of routine opt-out HIV testing in a female jail setting. The study was published in PLoS One, volume 4, issue 11, e7648. 27. Duffus WA, Youmans E (2009) highlighted missed opportunities for early HIV diagnosis in correctional facilities. The study was published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs, volume 23, issue 12, pages 1025-1032. 28. Jafa K, McElroy P, et al. (2009) published findings in PLoS One, volume 4, issue 5, e5416. 29. Motshabi LC, Pengpid S, et al. (2011) examined HIV counseling and testing utilization and attitudes among male inmates in a South African prison. The study was published in the Journal of Social Aspects of HIV/AIDS, volume 8, issue 3, pages 107-114. 30. De Voux A, Spaulding AC, et al. (2012) provided empirical support for jail-based HIV testing in PLoS One, volume 7, issue 5, e37603. 31. UNODC, UNAIDS, WHO (2009) released a technical paper on HIV testing and counseling in prisons and closed settings. 32. Beckwith CG, Liu T, et al. (2010) analyzed HIV risk behavior before and after counseling and testing in jail. The study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes, volume 53, issue 4, pages 485-490. 33. MacGowan R, Margolis A, et al. (2009) evaluated voluntary rapid HIV testing in jails. The study was published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases, volume 36, supplement 2, pages S9-S13. 34. Beckwith CG, Bazerman L, et al. (2011) assessed a routine opt-out rapid HIV testing program in Rhode Island. The study was published in AIDS Education and Prevention, volume 23, issue 3, pages 96-109. 35. Tartaro C, Levy MP (2012) evaluated an HIV testing program in a jail setting, providing results and recommendations. The study was published in The Prison Journal, volume 93, issue 1, pages 57-79. 36. Andrinopoulos K, Kerrigan D, et al. (2010) established an HIV/STD program and assessed infection prevalence among incarcerated men in Jamaica. The study was published in the International Journal of STD and AIDS, volume 21, issue 2, pages 114-119. 37. Arp W (2009) examined the intersection of race, incarceration, and HIV/AIDS in Louisiana, emphasizing risky sexual behavior and mandatory testing. The study was published in Race, Class, and Gender, volume 16, issues 1-2, pages 228-237. 38. Kavasery R, Maru DS, et al. (2009) conducted a prospective controlled trial of routine opt-out HIV testing in a men’s jail. The study was published in PLoS One, volume 4, issue 11, e8056. 39. Strick LB, MacGowan J, et al. (2011) reported on HIV screening of male inmates during prison intake medical evaluations in Washington from 2006 to 2010. The findings were published in MMWR, volume 60, issue 24, pages 811-813. 40. Javanbakht M, Murphy R, et al. (2007) assessed the prevalence of sexually transmitted infections and HIV among incarcerated men who have sex with men from 2000 to 2005. The study was published in Sexually Transmitted Infections, volume 36, supplement 2, pages S17-S21. 41. Tuli K, Kerndt PR (2009) conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of preventing sexually transmitted infections among incarcerated men who have sex with men. The study was published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases, volume 36, supplement 2, pages S41-S48. 42. Roberson DW, White BL (2009) identified factors influencing adherence to antiretroviral therapy among HIV-infected female inmates. The study was published in the Journal of the Association of Nurses in AIDS Care, volume 20, issue 1, pages 50-61. 43. Small W, Wood E, et al. (2009) explored the impact of incarceration on adherence to HIV treatment among HIV-positive injection drug users. The study was published in AIDS Care, volume 21, issue 6, pages 708-714. 44. Shalihu N, Pretorius L, et al. (2014) described barriers to HIV antiretroviral therapy adherence among Namibian prisoners. The study was published in AIDS Care, ahead of print. 45. Catz SL, Thibodeau L, et al. (2011) identified prevention needs of HIV-positive men and women awaiting release from prison. The study was published in AIDS Behavior, volume 16, issue 1, pages 108-120. 46. Fontana L, Beckerman A (2007) examined primary care treatment needs and experiences of recently released individuals with HIV/AIDS. The study was published in the Journal of Health Care for the Poor and Underserved, volume 18, issue 3, pages 699-714. 47. Wohl DA, Scheyett A, et al. (2011) compared intensive case management with comprehensive pre-release discharge planning for linking HIV-infected prisoners to care. The study was published in AIDS Behavior, volume 15, issue 2, pages 356-364. 48. Nunn A, Cornwall A, et al. (2010) assessed the COMPASS program, which links HIV-positive jail inmates to treatment, care, and social services after release. The study was published in the Journal of Urban Health, volume 87, issue 6, pages 954-968. 49. Zaller ND, Holmes L, et al. (2008) evaluated linkage to treatment and supportive services among HIV-positive ex-offenders in Project Bridge. The study was published in the Journal of Health Care for the Poor and Underserved, volume 19, issue 2, pages 522-531. 50. Seal DW, Margolis AD, et al. (2008) examined substance use and sexual behavior during incarceration among men aged 18-29, including prevalence and correlates. The study was published in AIDS Behavior, volume 12, issue 1, pages 27-40. 51. Milloy MJ, Kerr T, et al. (2013) found that incarceration is associated with used syringe lending among active injection drug users with detectable plasma HIV-1 RNA. The study was published in BMC Infectious Diseases, volume 13, article 565. 52. Moller LF, Van Den Bergh BJ, et al. (2008) studied the effects of health promotion on drug use among prisoners in Kyrgyzstan. The study was published in the International Journal of Prisoner Health, volume 4, issue 3, pages 124-133. 53. Roshanfekr P, Farnia M, et al. (2013) evaluated the effectiveness of harm reduction programs in seven Iranian prisons. The study was published in the Iranian Journal of Public Health, volume 42, issue 12, pages 1430-1437. 54. Ferrer-Castro V, Crespo-Leiro MR, et al. (2012) reviewed a ten-year experience of a needle exchange program at Pereiro de Aguiar prison in Spain. The study was published in the Spanish Journal of Penitentiary Health, volume 14, issue 1, pages 3-11.
